tiles.name: angle
tiles.subtitle: MT6701
tiles.result: ANG = a sawtooth, -0.84 V to +0.84 V, once a turn of the shaft (0 at half a turn from the MT6701's zero)
notes: The MT6701's analog output (0-3.3 V a turn) less 1.65 V, times 0.51, by an OPA810: the shaft's angle without SSI.
Its zero is the MT6701's (set by its registers over the SSI, or where the magnet sits).

tiles.name: vibration
tiles.subtitle: OPA810
tiles.result: VIB = -the piezo's charge / 1 nF above 160 Hz: the motor's cogging, its commutation ripple, the bearing
notes: A piezo disc on the terminal into an OPA810 charge amplifier (1 nF, 1 M: from 160 Hz).  Stick the disc to the motor's
mount: the cogging at 12 a turn, the commutation's ripple, the bearing, the frame's resonances.

tiles.name: index
tiles.subtitle: QRE1113
tiles.result: IDX = 4.7 k x the sensor's current: a pulse once a turn as a white mark on the bell's rim passes
notes: The QRE1113 under the gimbal's rim (on b5), its collector held at 0 V by an OPA810: IDX = 4.7 k x Ic.  Put a white mark
(tape, paint) on the bell's lower rim: an index pulse a turn, a tachometer with no encoder.

tiles.name: motor supply
tiles.subtitle: 5-12 V in
tiles.result: VMOT = the larger of the barrel jack (5-12 V) and USB 5 V, each less a Schottky's 0.3-0.5 V; VM jack VMOT / 16
notes: Barrel jack (centre +), 5-12 V, through an SS34 into VMOT, as is USB's 5 V, so VMOT is about 4.6 V with no supply.
SMBJ12A and 220 uF on VMOT take the braking energy a motor returns.  VM: VMOT / 16 at high impedance.

tiles.name: halls
tiles.subtitle: DRV5055A3
tiles.result: HA, HB = 9.75 mV/mT from the two halls under the rotor: two sinusoids 120 electrical degrees apart as it turns
notes: Two DRV5055A3 under the gimbal's magnets (b5), 17.1 degrees apart (120 electrical for 7 pole pairs); each less half its
5 V, times 0.39 (as AMOD-M's m9).  The rotor's electrical angle without the encoder; hall-sensored commutation.

tiles.name: gimbal
tiles.subtitle: MT6701
tiles.result: the MT6701's angle on SSI (14 bits a turn) and as a sawtooth to b7; two hall signals 120 electrical degrees apart to b10; an index pulse to b9
notes: A GBM2804H-100T class gimbal motor on four slots over an MT6701 (SSI on the Pmod; DO through b6's buffer onto MISO);
a 6 x 2.5 mm diametric magnet on the shaft 0.5-2 mm above it.  Two DRV5055A3 under the magnets, a QRE1113 under the rim.

tiles.name: power
tiles.subtitle: USB-C 5 V in: +5, -5, +3.3 out
tiles.result: +5 V from the USB-C (up to 1.5 A), -5 V at 40 mA, +3.3 V at 300 mA; the green LED says 5 V is in, the red one that -5 V is up
notes: USB-C power only: 5.1 k on each CC asks any source for 5 V.  A 2 A PTC, a 5 V TVS (clamps at 9.2 V) and 20 uF.
The LM2664 charge pump makes -5 V for the op-amp tiles (40 mA: four tiles at 10 mA); it is not switched per tile, an op
amp with its +5 V removed draws nothing.  The TPS7A2033 makes 3.3 V for the comparator and the lines that meet the FPGA.
The socket along the top carries +5, ground, -5, ground, +3.3: the bench's rails for a breadboard experiment.

tiles.name: IMU
tiles.subtitle: LSM6DSO
tiles.result: six axes on SPI (the tutorial's gateware reads them): with the board on edge, the roll about the motor's axis
notes: LSM6DSO on SPI (mode 3): CS IMU on IO8, SCK IO4, MOSI IO7, MISO IO3, shared with the encoder through a 74LVC1G125
(CS ENC on IO6).  Gyro to 2000 dps, accelerometer to 16 g, to 6.66 kHz.  On edge: a one-axis gimbal's level reference.

tiles.name: bus current
tiles.subtitle: INA181
tiles.result: I = the driver's supply current, 1 V/A (+-1.2 A), negative while the motor brakes
notes: VMOT through 0.1 ohm to the driver; an INA181A1 (2.5 V on REF) and an OPA810 give I = 1 V/A both ways.  With VM: the
electrical power in; against the phase currents: the driver's losses; negative while the motor's energy comes back.

tiles.name: back-EMF
tiles.subtitle: OPA2171
tiles.result: EA, EB = phase A's and B's voltage / 14 against the neutral: with COAST high and the motor spun, its back-EMF
notes: Each phase through 13 k / 1 k; with every phase floating the three dividers are the motor's ground, so EA and EB read the
back-EMF against the neutral (14 x EA in volts).  Followed by an OPA2171.  A spun gimbal motor makes a few volts.

tiles.name: BLDC driver
tiles.subtitle: DRV8311H
tiles.result: the motor's phases at the duty cycles of IO5, IO1, IO2 (A, B, C); IA, IB = phase A's and B's currents (low side), 0.75 V/A; COAST high floats them
notes: DRV8311H in 3x PWM from VMB: INHA IO5, INHB IO1, INHC IO2; EN from COAST through a TLV3501 (high: every phase floats).
IA, IB = SOA, SOB shifted to 0 by 3.3 k / 10 k to -5 V: 0.75 V/A from 2.5 k while each low side conducts.  The motor on the terminal: C, B, A from the left.

tiles.name: phase current
tiles.subtitle: INA240
tiles.result: IPA = phase A's whole current, 1 V/A both ways, through every PWM state (compare b3's IA: the low side only)
notes: Phase A through 0.05 ohm between the driver and the motor; an INA240A1 (PWM rejection, common mode to 80 V) about 2.5 V
and an OPA810 that takes the 2.5 V away: IPA = 1 V/A, the whole current.  b3's IA sees only the low side's share.

back_text: 5-12 V on b2; USB-C 5 V on b1.
